title: Microsoft Delays Default Copilot Usage-Based Billing To Dec. 1, Adds Spending Cap Option
key_facts: Microsoft has delayed default usage-based billing (UBB) for new Microsoft 365 Copilot Business subscriptions bought through its Cloud Solution Provider (CSP) reseller programme: originally 2 Nov, now 1 Dec 2026.
On 2 Nov Microsoft will instead open Partner Center sandbox environments so resellers can test UBB.
Copilot Business licences get an adjustable default spending limit of 4,000 Copilot Credits (about $40) per user per month; partners can set it to zero to turn UBB off.
Copilot Business plans cost $18 to $32 per user per month; advanced AI use is billed on consumption on top, and the products covered include Copilot Cowork, Work IQ APIs and GitHub Copilot Harness.
UBB will roll out first in unnamed 'supported markets'; Australia, Belgium, Brazil, France, Germany, India, Italy, Korea, the Netherlands, Poland and Spain will not initially support it.
The reseller or partner that receives the bill is ultimately responsible for all charges on the CSP account, including unexpected consumption.
Users who hit the limit can ask for more, and administrators approve or refuse; IT administrators can also keep Copilot Credits and UBB switched off.
Microsoft changed its 'Copilot in 30' trial rules: customers with existing Copilot seats are no longer eligible.
quote_evidence: Originally set to start Nov. 2, usage-based billing (UBB) by default is now set to start Dec. 1, according to the Redmond, Wash.-based vendor.
Along with the rollout delay, Microsoft revealed that partners will have a default billing cap of 4,000 Copilot Credits—about $40—per user per month for M365 Copilot Business licenses.
Partners can set the spending limit to zero to turn off usage-based billing.
why_it_matters_hint: Resellers and their small-business customers get about a month more and a default spending limit before pay-per-use AI billing is switched on by default.
event_date: Not stated for the delay itself; CRN says Microsoft updated its FAQ on Wednesday (30 Sep 2026) and its Copilot Credits Guide on Thursday (1 Oct 2026); CRN published 2 Oct 2026.
notes: Continues the CRN story of 1 Oct 2026 (pool item 1001:C02-04, 'Microsoft Enables Consumption Billing By Default For Copilot Business'). New today: the delay to 1 Dec, the 4,000-credit default cap, the sandbox date, the list of countries left out. All details come from Microsoft documents as relayed by CRN. Exact date of the delay announcement not stated.
